Vintergatan.text: The Milky Way. From soft pads to heavy bass, with wavetables to draw and shape and modulation you drag onto any knob. Opens your Serum and Vital presets.

Norrsken.text: The northern lights. A bright, immediate synth for leads, stabs and pads, with a face made to be played.

Mini Moonbeam.text: Three oscillators into a ladder filter, for basses and leads with weight.

Shy One.text: One oscillator with a sub, a filter and an arpeggiator. Small, quick and made for basslines.

Two-Filter Mono.text: A high-pass and a low-pass filter that both sing, and two oscillators with a raw edge.

Titan 303.text: One oscillator, a squelching filter and an accent, for acid lines.

June Bloom.text: One oscillator a voice with a sub, and a chorus that makes it wide.

Juniper Eight.text: Eight voices of two oscillators, layered or split across the keys, with an arpeggiator.

Promise Bloom.text: Five voices of two oscillators, with poly-mod for bells, brass and sweeps.

String Ensemble.text: Bass and upper sections, from cello to choir, through a rich ensemble.

Jet-8000.text: Eight voices in two parts, with seven oscillator modes, sync and cross modulation.

Six-Op FM.text: Six operators and their algorithms, for electric pianos, bells and basses that cut. Opens the original's voice banks.

SID.text: Three voices with the sound of an 8-bit home computer's chip: pulse, sync, ring modulation and a shared filter.

Reed Electric Piano.text: Felt hammers on steel reeds, with tremolo and the bark of a driven preamp.

Tine Electric Piano.text: Hammers on tines, a bell in the attack and a stereo vibrato.

Electric Clavichord.text: Struck strings and their pickups, from soft to brilliant, for funk that bites.

Tonewheel Organ.text: Ninety-one tonewheels, drawbars, percussion and a chorus-vibrato.

Leviathan Rig.text: A heavy rig in one device: gate, overdrive, distortion, amp, EQ and cabinet, each switched by itself.

Djent Amp.text: Tight and heavy: a drive with its own attack, three amp channels, EQ and cabinet.

Untitled Amp.text: Gate, drive and boost into an amp with two gains, then EQ and cabinet.

Green Overdrive Pedal.text: Lifts the middle of your guitar into two diodes, for a singing push into an amp.

Metal District Pedal.text: High gain with an equaliser of its own, from scooped to a wall of mids.

Lift Pedal.text: One transistor that raises the level and the edge of an amp.

Saucer Fuzz.text: Two transistors, germanium or silicon, from smooth to sputtering.

Mitten Fuzz.text: Four stages of soft clipping and a tone stack, for sustain without end.

Burrow Distortion.text: An op-amp that narrows as you turn it up, from crunch to grind.

Squash Compressor.text: Evens your playing out, for clean funk and country picking.

Whiny Shifter.text: An expression pedal sweeps the pitch between a heel and a toe interval.

Hush Gate.text: Shuts the hiss of a driven amp between notes.

Comet Flanger.text: A bucket-brigade flanger for guitars, keys, drums and whole mixes.

Memento Delay.text: A bucket-brigade echo, with chorus or vibrato on its repeats.

Teardrop Wah.text: A resonant peak swept by the pedal, an envelope or an LFO.

Quack Filter.text: The auto-wah, for funk guitar, clav and bass.

Clementine Phaser.text: Four stages and one knob, for guitars and electric pianos.

Neon Tremolo.text: A lamp and a photocell, pulsing like an old amplifier's tremolo.

Leveltron Opto.text: A lamp and a photocell turn the level down, smooth and slow, through a valve amplifier.

Danish Blue Compressor.text: Optical compression with a valve make-up stage: fixed, manual or both.

Quickdraw FET.text: A field-effect transistor clamps the peaks fast, its ratios on buttons.

Desk Glue Bus Compressor.text: Glues a mix bus or a drum group together.

Mid-Century Vari-Mu.text: Valves that turn down gently, for masters and drum buses.

Blower Box.text: Compression and valve heat in one, for drums, bass and buses.

Push-Pull EQ.text: Boost and cut the same band at once, through a valve make-up amplifier.

Not Out Class A.text: A class-A console channel with its transformers, for shaping single tracks.

Mid-Century Preamp.text: Two triode stages and a transformer, for warmth on any track.

Swiss Roll Tape.text: Onto tape and back: saturation, wow, flutter and hiss.

June Chorus.text: Two delay lines of capacitors, for wide synths and clean guitars.

Rotary Speaker.text: A horn and a drum that spin at speeds of their own: slow, fast or stopped.

Moonladder.text: A transistor ladder low-pass filter for any track.

Filter.text: Ladders, a diode ladder and more, with an LFO and an envelope follower.

Low Orbit Echo.text: A loop of tape past three playback heads, with a spring reverb after them.

Gemini Plate.text: A sheet of steel under tension, its decay set by a damper.

Drip Spring.text: Two or three springs in a tank, as in a guitar amp.

1978 Digital Hall.text: A hall reverb of the late 1970s, modelled as its algorithm.

1976 Digital Reverb.text: The first digital reverb, of the mid-1970s, with its echo programs.

1981 Digital Ambience.text: An early-1980s digital reverb with its plates, halls and rooms.

Anchor Arpeggiator.text: An arpeggio in two parts: an anchor on the chord's notes and a line that moves around it.

Twin Arpeggiator.text: Two arpeggiators side by side, each over its own range of keys.

Chord Pads.text: Sixteen chords on pads, from sets in many styles or written by hand.

Bassline Maker.text: A bass line from an on-beat and an off-beat phrase, varied at a click.

Chord Steps.text: A polyphonic step sequencer, kept in a scale.

Pattern Variations.text: Plays a pattern of steps and makes variations of it at a click.

Euclidean Notes.text: Four lines of Euclidean rhythms whose notes wander in a scale.

Rhythm Map.text: A map of rhythms: move across it and the beat changes.

Drum Grid.text: Eight channels of sixteen steps, each a drum.

Note Repeater.text: Repeats each note like a delay, its velocity and pitch moving as it goes.

Key Chords.text: Keeps notes to a scale, and turns one note into a chord.

Note Filter.text: Lets through the notes you want, and changes their pitch, length and velocity.

Note Chance.text: Lets notes through by chance or by a pattern, and varies them.

Kick.text: A kick drum built from five layers, a body, a click, noise or a sample, each shaped over the hit by curves of pitch and level.
